question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: Vectors are graded in order, i = 0 … total-1, where total is the number of vectors; gots[i] past the end of gots is the absent value and gots beyond the vectors are ignored. pass = the number of vectors for which PASS(gots[i], expected) holds. miss = the names of the failing vectors in order, cut to the first 8 (names repeat when vectors repeat them). full = (pass equals total); an empty vector list gives pass 0, total 0, full true, miss empty. A throw anywhere in R5–R13 while grading any vector makes the WHOLE call throw (no partial result); vectors before it do not soften that.
THROWN(x): x is a map (not a list, not none, not a scalar) that has an OWN key __throw. The key's value is not inspected (text, a number, none) and other keys may be present.

PASS(g, e) = THROWN(g) and THROWN(e), or else SAME(g, e). When both are thrown, e is never decoded — so a malformed tag inside a thrown expected cannot throw; a thrown got against an unthrown expected falls through to SAME, and so does an unthrown got against a thrown expected (which is decoded, and may throw, R6).

SAME(g, e): CANON(g) and CANON(REVIVE(e)) are the identical ordered tree. Lists compare element by element; maps compare entry by entry in KEY ORDER, keys and values both, with the same entry count; text by UTF-16 code units; finite numbers by value; bools; none. KEY ORDER of a map = its array-index keys (the canonical decimal spelling of an integer 0 … 4294967294) ascending first, then every other key in arrival order. So in the host slice {a:1, b:2} is not SAME as {b:2, a:1}, while {b:1, "1":2} is SAME as {"1":2, b:1} CITED FIDELITY package — eq compares serialized text, ext key-order call
CANON(v), applied recursively, first matching row of TABLE CANON. A tag map produced by CANON has its keys in the order the row lists them.
the absent value                                       | {__t: "undef"}
a big integer                                          | {__t: "bigint", v: its decimal text (a leading "-" when negative)}
the number -0                                          | {__t: "num", v: "-0"}
NaN, +Infinity, -Infinity                               | {__t: "num", v: "NaN" / "Infinity" / "-Infinity"}
a regular expression                                   | {__t: "regex", source: its normalized source, flags: its normalized flags} (R10)
a boxed wrapper                                        | {__t: "boxed", k: "Number" / "String" / "Boolean" by kind, v: CANON(its payload)}
a set                                                  | {__t: "set", values: CANON of each member in insertion order}
a keyed collection                                     | {__t: "map", entries: [CANON(key), CANON(value)] for each entry in insertion order}
a byte array                                           | {__t: "u8", bytes: its bytes as numbers 0–255, buf: whether it is buffer-flavoured}
a list with a hole (an index below its length absent)   | {__t: "sparse", length: its length, entries: [index, CANON(element)] for each present index ascending}
any other list                                         | the list of CANON of each element

a map                                                  | the map of the same keys in KEY ORDER with CANON values; when the ORIGINAL map has an OWN key __t, __throw or __threw (any value) it is wrapped as {__t: "obj", v: that map} CITED rederive selfhost #67 — own keys only
text, a finite number other than -0, a bool, none       | itself

REVIVE(e), recursively. A list -> the list of REVIVE of each element, holes kept as holes. A map whose key __t holds one of the texts of TABLE REVIVE -> that row (other keys of the tag map are ignored unless the row reads them). Any other map (no __t, or a __t of another text or a non-text value) -> a fresh map with the same keys in the same order and REVIVE of each value; its own __t stays as data, so CANON wraps it again (R5) and {__t: "zzz", a: 1} is SAME as itself. Text, numbers, bools, none, the absent value and a big integer -> themselves. A host set, keyed collection, regular expression, byte array or boxed wrapper reaching REVIVE (host slice only) is read as a map of its own enumerable keys: empty for a set, a keyed collection, a regular expression and a boxed number or bool; a byte array gives the keys "0" … "n-1" holding its bytes; a boxed text gives "0" … "n-1" holding its one-character texts CITED FIDELITY package — revive's plain-map branch takes any object; ext y0–y6: an expected set equals the got {}, and a set got never equals a set expected
__t "undef"   | the absent value
__t "regex"   | a regular expression from pattern t.source and flags t.flags; an absent pattern is the empty pattern, absent flags mean no flags (R10)
__t "bigint"  | a big integer from t.v (R11)
__t "num"     | t.v must be exactly one of the texts "NaN", "Infinity", "-Infinity", "-0" -> that number; any other t.v (other text, a number, absent) -> throws CITED rederive selfhost #55 (round 4)
__t "boxed"   | x = REVIVE(t.v); t.k "Number" -> boxed number TO-NUMBER(x); t.k "String" -> boxed text TO-TEXT(x); any other t.k ("Boolean", absent, anything) -> boxed bool TO-BOOL(x)
__t "set"     | a set of REVIVE of each element of t.values in order (R8); a falsy t.values (R7) is the empty list; a t.values that is truthy and not a list -> throws
__t "map"     | a keyed collection (R8) from t.entries read as in R9; a falsy t.entries is the empty list; truthy and not a list -> throws
__t "u8"      | a byte array from t.bytes (R12), buffer-flavoured when t.buf is truthy (R7)
__t "sparse"  | a list from t.length and t.entries (R13)

__t "obj"     | t.v must be a map (none, a list, a scalar or absent -> throws, CITED rederive selfhost #55); a fresh map of t.v's keys in order with REVIVE of each value — t.v's own __t, __throw, __threw are data, never a tag

TRUTHY: every value except false, 0, -0, NaN, the empty text, none and the absent value (an empty list and an empty map are truthy). TO-BOOL(x) = TRUTHY(x). TO-TEXT(x): text is itself; a number is its shortest round-trip digits, written in plain decimal notation when x is 0 or 1e-6 <= |x| < 1e21, else in scientific notation (the first digit, then "." and the remaining digits when there are any, then e+n or e-n): 5 -> "5", 0.5 -> "0.5", 1e21 -> "1e+21", 1.5e-7 -> "1.5e-7", -0 -> "0"; true/false -> "true"/"false"; none -> "null"; the absent value -> "undefined"; a list -> TO-TEXT of its elements joined by "," (a none or absent element gives the empty text); a map -> "[object Object]". TO-NUMBER(x): a number is itself; true/false -> 1/0; none -> 0; the absent value -> NaN; text -> after trimming WS from both ends, the empty text -> 0, a decimal literal (optional sign; digits, optionally then "." and zero or more digits, or "." then one or more digits; optional e/E exponent; or Infinity after the optional sign) or an unsigned 0x/0o/0b literal -> its value, anything else -> NaN; a list or a map -> TO-NUMBER(TO-TEXT(x)).

SET MEMBERS and COLLECTION KEYS are unique under SAME-VALUE-ZERO: NaN equals NaN, -0 equals 0 (and is stored as 0), text/number/bool/none/big integer/absent compare by value, every list or map is distinct (REVIVE builds fresh ones). A later duplicate member is dropped; a later duplicate key replaces the earlier entry's value and the entry keeps its first position.

COLLECTION ENTRIES: each element of t.entries is read as a pair by taking its first two items: a list gives its first and second elements (a missing one is the absent value; extra ones are ignored), a text gives its first and second characters (so "ab" is the pair "a", "b"); any other element (a number, none, a map, a bool) -> throws. Key and value are then REVIVE'd.

REGULAR EXPRESSIONS: flags (when present, read as text: none is the text "null") is a set of letters from d g i m s u v y, each at most once, u and v not together; anything else -> throws. Normalized flags = those letters in the order d g i m s u v y. The pattern (read as text) must be valid in the host dialect (the js file's pin) or -> throws. Its normalized source: the empty pattern is "(?:)", an unescaped "/" becomes "\/", a line feed becomes the two characters "\n" (the host's source-escaping, the js file's pin).

BIG INTEGER from t.v: text, after trimming WS from both ends — the empty text is 0; an optional sign then decimal digits; or (no sign) 0x/0o/0b then digits of that base; anything else -> throws. A number that is an integer -> that integer; a non-integer number -> throws. true/false -> 1/0. A list or a map -> the text rule applied to TO-TEXT of it ([5] -> 5, [] -> 0, a map -> throws). none or the absent value -> throws.

BYTES from t.bytes: a list -> one byte per element, TO-NUMBER of it, NaN and ±Infinity -> 0, otherwise truncated toward zero and reduced modulo 256 into 0–255 (256 -> 0, -1 -> 255, 1.5 -> 1, "7" -> 7, "a" -> 0, none -> 0, true -> 1). A text -> when buffer-flavoured, its UTF-8 bytes ("12" -> 49, 50); otherwise one byte per character by the list rule ("12" -> 1, 2). A number -> the empty byte array when not buffer-flavoured, throws when buffer-flavoured. The absent value -> throws (either flavour).

HOLED LISTS from t.length and t.entries: a t.length that is a number must be an integer in 0 … 4294967295 (else throws) and starts a list of that many holes; an absent t.length starts the one-element list [absent value]; any other t.length (text, a bool, none, a map) starts the one-element list [t.length] (not revived) CITED FIDELITY package — p2, p3, p5, v7 Then each element of t.entries (a falsy t.entries is the empty list; a text t.entries is read as the list of its characters; any other truthy non-list -> throws) is a pair [i, x] read as in R9 (an element that cannot be read as a pair -> throws): i (a number or an index text like "1") puts REVIVE(x) at index i, extending the length when i is at or past it; an i that is not an array index (negative) puts nothing visible; a later pair for the same index overwrites. A list without holes then spells as a plain list (R5).
